items.title: Domain Health Checker
items.description: DNS, TLS, HTTP, email security, recommendations, and exports.
items.rationale: Core troubleshooting workflow for IT admins and MSP engineers.

items.title: DNS Record Checker
items.description: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME, SOA, SPF, and DMARC lookups.
items.rationale: Fast public DNS inspection without storing queried domains.

items.title: SSL Certificate Checker
items.description: Certificate subject, issuer, SANs, dates, and expiration status.
items.rationale: Helps catch certificate incidents before renewal windows are missed.

items.title: HTTP Status Checker
items.description: Status, redirects, response timing, headers, and security hints.
items.rationale: Useful first-pass check for public websites and APIs.

items.title: JSON Formatter, Base64, JWT, and Cron tools
items.description: Everyday text utilities for public-safe troubleshooting.
items.rationale: Keeps common admin tasks in one fast toolkit.

items.title: Azure AI log summaries
items.description: Optional Azure AI summary for sanitized log troubleshooting submissions.
items.rationale: Adds contextual help while preserving opt-in, sanitized-only behavior.

items.title: GitHub-connected roadmap board
items.description: Public board that merges curated seeds with public GitHub feature requests.
items.rationale: Makes priorities visible and gives users a clear path to suggest improvements. Status was stale at "In Progress" -- utils/roadmap.py's load_roadmap_board() already merges seed items with live GitHub issues (source-tagged Seed vs GitHub #N) and pages/10_Roadmap_Feedback.py renders the combined board with a working Submit Idea link. Found while auditing the full roadmap list, not built this round.

items.title: Downloadable HTML reports
items.description: Export polished standalone HTML reports from Domain Health checks.
items.rationale: MSPs can share findings with customers without extra formatting work.

items.title: More DNS and email security checks
items.description: Expand SPF, DMARC, DNSSEC, MTA-STS, and SMTP TLS reporting in Domain Health.
items.rationale: Email security posture is a recurring operational need.

items.title: One-off uptime and latency trend visualization
items.description: Show short-lived trend charts without storing historical checks.
items.rationale: Gives context during incident checks while keeping the app persistence-free. Shipped as a new Uptime Trend tool: runs 3-20 sequential HTTP checks against a URL in a single page render, with an optional delay between checks, and plots latency + uptime % as a plotly chart. Every sample lives only in that one script run's return value -- nothing is written to disk, a database, or session state that survives the page. Capped checks/interval to keep it from being usable as a load-testing tool against third parties, with an explicit warning in the page copy.

items.title: GitHub reaction-based voting
items.description: Use GitHub issue reactions as the real vote source for feature ideas.
items.rationale: Keeps feedback public and avoids adding a custom database. Status was stale at "Planned" -- utils/roadmap.py's github_issue_to_roadmap_item() already reads reactions.total_count from the GitHub Issues API response and uses it directly as votes for GitHub-sourced roadmap items (covered by tests/test_roadmap.py). Found while auditing the full roadmap list, not built this round.

items.title: AI-generated remediation checklists
items.description: Turn safe rule-based findings into short action checklists.
items.rationale: Recommended because it builds on existing findings without requiring raw secret input. The rule-based findings and safe_next_steps already existed on the Log Troubleshooting Assistant; changed the last piece -- next steps rendered as plain bullet text -- into actual interactive st.checkbox items per finding, so it's a literal checklist a visitor can tick through rather than just a list.

items.title: AI-assisted feature triage for maintainers
items.description: Summarize GitHub feature requests for maintainers in an admin workflow.
items.rationale: Could help prioritize user ideas later, but should remain opt-in and secret-safe. Shipped on the Roadmap & Feedback page: an opt-in "Summarize with AI" button (only enabled when Azure OpenAI is configured) sends the open (not-Complete) roadmap items' public fields -- titles, descriptions, vote counts, already visible on the page -- to produce a short prioritization summary. No dedicated admin login exists in this app (it's fully public with no auth system), so the practical maintainer gate is the same one already used by the Log Troubleshooting Assistant's AI opt-in: the feature only activates when the maintainer configures their own Azure OpenAI credentials. Cached for 1 hour (st.cache_data) so repeated clicks by any visitor reuse one AI call rather than each paying for a fresh one. Also fixed a stale claim on the same page ("This page does not call Azure/OpenAI") that this feature would have made false.

items.title: Tool bundle recommendations
items.description: Suggest the next tool to run based on current troubleshooting context.
items.rationale: Helps users move from DNS to SSL to HTTP checks without a heavy workflow engine. Shipped as a curated (not AI-generated) TOOL_BUNDLES map in utils/ui.py -- hand-picked "what would you naturally run next" pairings, e.g. DNS Record Checker -> Domain Health Checker/WHOIS/SSL, JWT Decoder -> JWT Encoder/Hash Generator. A "Related tools" row renders after a tool's own result via tool_result_panel(..., related_to=<slug>). No heavy workflow engine, matching the rationale; a tool with no natural next step is simply absent from the map rather than forced into one.

items.title: ConnectWise and PSA export ideas
items.description: Explore lightweight exports that can be pasted into ticketing systems.
items.rationale: MSP users often need customer-ready notes after troubleshooting. Shipped as a "PSA / ticket note" export on Domain Health Checker and Log Troubleshooting Assistant -- plain text with no markdown syntax (# and ** render literally in most PSA ticket note fields, unlike the existing Markdown export), shown via a copy-button st.code block plus a .txt download. Deliberately not a direct ConnectWise Manage/Autotask API integration -- that needs per-tenant API credentials this public, no-storage app has nowhere safe to hold; a copy-paste-ready plain-text note fits the "lightweight exports" framing in the description without that scope.

items.title: Command palette / quick-jump launcher
items.description: A keyboard-triggered launcher to jump straight to any tool, complementing the sidebar quick-search.
items.rationale: Power users on killer-tools-style sites expect a Ctrl+K-style jump; the sidebar search covers most of this need today but isn't reachable by keyboard shortcut. NOT flatly blocked like the PWA item, but not attempted this round either: unlike a real service worker, a global keydown listener + overlay is plausibly buildable via the same same-origin iframe trick this app already uses for the localStorage mirror (the iframe can reach window.top.document, so it could attach a listener and DOM-inject an overlay there). But it's a materially bigger and more fragile JS surface than anything shipped so far -- real DOM manipulation of the top-level page from inside an iframe script, a hand-built filter/keyboard-nav overlay, dark/light theme handling, focus trapping -- and this sandboxed dev environment has no real browser to visually verify any of it before it ships to a live auto-deploying site. Left open rather than built blind; worth a manual-verification pass with browser access, not a routine PR.

items.title: Drag-to-reorder favorites
items.description: Shipped as move-earlier/move-later buttons on each Favorites card, not literal mouse drag. True drag-and-drop needs a bidirectional Streamlit custom component with a JS build step this repo doesn't have; the existing one-way iframe-to-URL trick used elsewhere in the app would mean a full page reload per drag, which is worse UX than buttons. Reorder controls only appear on the visitor's own Favorites grid, never on the read-only Shared Favorites grid.
items.rationale: Favorites currently keep insertion order; manual reordering is a small, self-contained UX add-on once favorites are already shipped.

items.title: WHOIS lookup tool
items.description: Public WHOIS/RDAP registration lookup alongside the existing DNS and SSL checkers.
items.rationale: A natural companion to Domain Health and DNS tools for the same troubleshooting workflow.

items.title: Regex tester
items.description: Test a pattern against sample text with match positions and groups, guarded by a hard evaluation timeout against catastrophic backtracking.
items.rationale: Common everyday utility that fits the existing text-tools family (JSON, Base64, JWT).

items.title: URL encoder/decoder
items.description: Encode/decode URL components and query strings, similar to the existing Base64 tool.
items.rationale: Frequently needed alongside Base64/JWT when debugging webhooks and API calls.

items.title: Password / passphrase generator
items.description: Generate strong random passwords or diceware-style passphrases locally, never transmitted.
items.rationale: High-demand, low-risk addition that fits the public-safe, no-storage positioning well.

items.title: Certificate chain validator
items.description: Diagnose chain trust issues (missing intermediate, self-signed, expired, hostname mismatch) on the SSL Certificate Checker. Scoped to OpenSSL verify-code diagnosis rather than full leaf-to-root enumeration, since Python's stdlib ssl module can't walk the full chain before 3.13.
items.rationale: Extends the existing SSL Certificate Checker beyond leaf-certificate details.

items.title: Bulk Domain Health checks via CSV upload
items.description: Upload a list of domains and run Domain Health across all of them, exporting one combined report.
items.rationale: MSPs managing many client domains currently have to run checks one at a time.

items.title: Shareable favorites link
items.description: A "Share favorites" popover on Home builds a copyable link (a new read-only shared_fav param) that renders the sender's list as a distinct "Shared Favorites" section for the recipient. Deliberately NOT built by reusing the existing fav param directly: that would have let opening a shared link silently overwrite the recipient's own saved favorites in localStorage, since the existing persistence mirror writes any fav value present in the URL straight into local storage. shared_fav is excluded from that mirror entirely.
items.rationale: Favorites already live in the URL's query params client-side; surfacing a share/copy action is a small extension of that mechanism.

items.title: Installable PWA / offline app shell
items.description: Add a web app manifest and service worker so the toolkit can be installed and its shell used offline.
items.rationale: Matches the "works everywhere" positioning already in the trust chips and feature strip. BLOCKED as scoped, verified against the installed streamlit==1.61.0 package source, not just platform folklore: Streamlit's only static-file-serving route is server.enableStaticServing, which mounts files at /app/static/{path} (streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py, _ROUTE_APP_STATIC), never at the origin root. A service worker registered from /app/static/sw.js can only control pages under /app/static/ by default (its scope is limited to its own directory unless the server sends a Service-Worker-Allowed header, which Streamlit's static handler has no way to set) -- so it could never actually control the live app pages, making a real installable/offline PWA unreachable through any Streamlit-native mechanism, independent of whatever Streamlit Cloud's proxy additionally restricts.

items.title: Accessibility audit pass
items.description: Computed WCAG contrast ratios across every theme-token text/background pairing and fixed two real AA failures: dark-theme muted/caption text (3.79:1 -> 4.59:1) and the "NEW" badge's white-on-green text (as low as 1.4:1 -> 5.4:1+). Scoped to color contrast, which is objectively verifiable from the CSS tokens without a browser; ARIA labeling and full keyboard-navigation testing need real browser/screen-reader verification this sandboxed environment can't provide, so they're left for a manual pass.
items.rationale: The site has grown a lot of custom CSS/components this cycle; a dedicated accessibility pass hasn't happened yet.

items.title: Webhook / HTTP request tester
items.description: Shipped the outbound half: send a one-off HTTP request with a custom method, headers, and body, and inspect the response. The originally scoped RequestBin-style inbound endpoint (capturing incoming webhook calls at a public URL) is a materially different feature -- it needs a real receiving endpoint and in-memory/session storage for arrivals, not just a request client -- so it's still open as a separate, larger idea rather than folded into this one.
items.rationale: Common need when debugging integrations; fits the toolkit's no-storage, public-safe model if payloads are ephemeral and session-scoped.

items.title: Timestamp / epoch converter
items.description: Convert between Unix epoch, ISO 8601, and human-readable timestamps across timezones, plus a live "now" reference.
items.rationale: One of the most common everyday IT utilities; surprisingly missing given the toolkit already has a Cron Explainer.

items.title: Text diff checker
items.description: Side-by-side or unified diff between two blocks of text, highlighting additions and removals.
items.rationale: Frequently needed alongside JSON/config troubleshooting to spot what changed between two versions.

items.title: JWT encoder
items.description: Build and sign a JWT from a JSON payload and secret using an HMAC algorithm, complementing the existing decode-only JWT Decoder.
items.rationale: Decoding already exists; encoding is the natural other half for testing auth flows locally.

items.title: CIDR / IP range aggregator
items.description: Summarize a list of IPs or CIDR blocks into the minimal set of covering supernets.
items.rationale: Extends the existing Subnet Calculator for firewall-rule and ACL cleanup work.

items.title: User-Agent string parser
items.description: Break a User-Agent header down into browser, OS, and device details.
items.rationale: Common companion lookup alongside HTTP Status Checker and Email Header Analyzer.

items.title: IPv6 address compressor/expander
items.description: Convert an IPv6 address between its compressed (::) and fully expanded form.
items.rationale: Small, frequently-needed complement to the Subnet Calculator and CIDR Aggregator.

items.title: Cron next-run calendar export
items.description: Export the Cron Explainer's next-run times as a downloadable .ics calendar file.
items.rationale: Lets users drop scheduled job times straight into their calendar instead of re-reading the explainer each time.

items.title: Slugify / case converter
items.description: Convert text between slug-case, camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and Title Case.
items.rationale: Everyday utility for developers naming files, variables, and URLs.

items.title: MAC vendor (OUI) lookup
items.description: Show the registered vendor/manufacturer for a MAC address's OUI prefix.
items.rationale: Natural extension of the existing MAC Address Tool -- the OUI is already parsed out, just not looked up.

items.title: Color code converter
items.description: Convert colors between HEX, RGB, and HSL, with a live swatch preview.
items.rationale: Common small utility for anyone touching CSS/UI work alongside the IT-focused tools.

items.title: RequestBin-style inbound webhook capture
items.description: A real ephemeral endpoint (e.g. /webhook/<session-id>) that captures incoming HTTP calls from third-party services and displays them live, with no persistent storage.
items.rationale: Split out from the original 'Webhook / HTTP request tester' idea once the outbound request-testing half shipped -- this inbound-capture half needs a real receiving endpoint and session-scoped in-memory storage, a bigger architectural lift than a single Streamlit page. BLOCKED as scoped: Streamlit Community Cloud (this app's deployment target) only runs `streamlit run app.py` behind its own proxy and exposes no way to register a custom HTTP route -- there is no in-app way to actually receive third-party POSTs. A monkey-patch of the underlying Tornado/Starlette handler list would touch the same server layer that caused a real production outage on this app before (the GZipResponder/starlette-version incident), and wouldn't be reachable through Streamlit Cloud's proxy anyway. This becomes buildable only if paired with a small separate receiver service (e.g. FastAPI on the Oracle VM this session runs on, behind nginx) that the Streamlit page reads from -- a new service and public endpoint, i.e. a real infrastructure decision, not a routine PR.

items.title: Security headers checker
items.description: Inspect a URL's HTTP response headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) and grade what's missing (A-F), similar to securityheaders.com.
items.rationale: Shipped as its own Security Headers Checker page, reusing the same request pattern as HTTP Status Checker/Webhook Tester. Grading also flags weak (not just missing) HSTS max-age and permissive CSP values, not just presence/absence.

items.title: DKIM selector lookup
items.description: Given a domain and a DKIM selector, query and parse the DKIM TXT record (public key, key type, flags) the same way SPF/DMARC are already checked.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated DKIM Selector Lookup page. Since a DKIM record's location depends on a selector that isn't discoverable from DNS alone, the form takes both domain and selector explicitly, then queries <selector>._domainkey.<domain> and parses the v=/k=/p= fields. Reuses dns_tools.get_resolver/txt_to_string (made public alongside record_to_row for this).

items.title: DNS propagation checker
items.description: Query the same DNS record type across several public resolvers (Google 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Quad9 9.9.9.9) side by side to catch propagation lag or mismatched answers after a DNS change.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated DNS Propagation Checker page. Queries Google (8.8.8.8), Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), and Quad9 (9.9.9.9) directly via dnspython's per-resolver nameserver override, and compares the sorted answer sets to flag propagation lag or mismatch. Refactored dns_tools.record_to_row from a private helper to a public one so both DNS Record Checker and this tool share the same record-formatting logic.

items.title: IP geolocation lookup
items.description: Resolve an IP address to approximate geography, ASN, and network/ISP info via a public API, mirroring the pattern already used for MAC vendor lookup.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated IP Geolocation Lookup page against the free ip-api.com public API (no key). Chose it over ipapi.co after live testing -- ipapi.co's free tier hit its rate limit on back-to-back sequential test calls, while ip-api.com handled repeated calls cleanly with clear success/fail states (including distinct 'private range' and 'invalid query' messages). Also caught and fixed a real bug during interactive verification: passing mixed-type values (strings and floats) straight into a bare pd.DataFrame triggers a PyArrow serialization warning/auto-fix in Streamlit -- switched to the existing display_rows_frame() helper (utils/ui.py), which already exists specifically for this.

items.title: File hash / integrity comparator
items.description: Upload two files (or a file plus an expected hash string) and compare their digests to confirm a download wasn't corrupted or tampered with.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated File Integrity Comparator page. Extends the existing Hash Generator (text-only) to file uploads: compare two uploaded files directly, or check one file against a pasted expected hash (auto-matched across MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, case-insensitive). Stdlib hashlib only, capped at 100MB per file to avoid memory pressure on Streamlit Cloud.

items.title: Cron expression builder
items.description: The reverse of the existing Cron Explainer: pick a schedule via simple minute/hour/day controls and get the resulting cron expression, instead of typing one in to be explained.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated Cron Expression Builder page with per-field Every/Every N/Specific controls. Reuses the existing explain_cron() from utils/text_tools.py (already used by Cron Explainer) to validate the built expression and preview its readable description and next run times, keeping the two pages consistent rather than reimplementing cron semantics. Live-updates, no submit button -- same no-vanishing-risk pattern as chmod Calculator and Integer Base Converter.

items.title: Incident message formatter for Slack/Teams
items.description: Turn the current Domain Health / Uptime Trend results into a ready-to-paste Slack or Teams incident-update message (their respective mrkdwn/Adaptive-Card-safe plain formatting), the same way the PSA/ticket-note export already avoids raw markdown symbols.
items.rationale: Shipped as new export sections on the existing Domain Health Checker and Uptime Trend pages (not a standalone page, since it turns those pages' own results into a message). Reuses the PSA-note plain-text-summary pattern in utils/reporting.py but produces Slack mrkdwn (single-asterisk bold) or Teams/GFM-style markdown (double-asterisk bold) via tabs -- st.tabs specifically, not a radio/selectbox, because a rerun-triggering widget outside st.form would have hit the same vanishing-results bug fixed in PR #33/#34.

items.title: QR code generator
items.description: Generate a QR code for a URL, Wi-Fi credentials, or plain text/contact info, for onboarding handoffs and support materials.
items.rationale: Shipped as a QR Code Generator page with two tabs: plain text/URL, and Wi-Fi credentials (WIFI: payload format most phone cameras recognize directly, with proper backslash-escaping of special characters in SSID/password per the format spec). Adds qrcode as a new dependency; Pillow was already a transitive dependency (streamlit itself needs it for st.image), so this only adds the one package. Live-updates, no submit button -- no results-vanishing risk.

items.title: Windows Event ID reference
items.description: Searchable reference of common Windows Event Log IDs with description, source, and severity, similar to killertools.net's Windows Event Lookup.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated Windows Event Reference page, same static-dataset + search shape as the existing Port Reference. Curated set of ~38 commonly-triaged event IDs across System/Application/Security/PowerShell logs, each with log, source, severity, summary, and common cause.

items.title: Windows/Win32 error code lookup
items.description: Look up a Windows error code (hex or decimal) -- system errors, BSOD stop codes, WMI/RPC/MSI errors -- and get the plain-language meaning.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated Windows Error Reference page, same static-dataset + search shape as Windows Event Reference and Port Reference. Curated set of ~62 codes across Win32, Service Control, RPC, HRESULT, and NTSTATUS/BSOD categories, searchable by decimal code, hex code, category, or keyword.

items.title: M365 license SKU decoder
items.description: Convert Microsoft 365 license SKU strings and GUIDs (e.g. SPE_E3, ENTERPRISEPACK) to readable product names.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated M365 SKU Decoder page. All 42 entries were verified directly against Microsoft's official licensing CSV (learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/users/licensing-service-plan-reference) rather than reconstructed from memory -- an initial memory-based draft and a lossy AI-summarized page fetch both produced several wrong/swapped GUIDs, caught only by cross-checking against the raw authoritative CSV before shipping.

items.title: CVE lookup
items.description: Search the NIST National Vulnerability Database by CVE ID or keyword and show severity, description, and affected products.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated CVE Lookup page against the live NIST NVD public API (no API key required for this usage level). Supports exact CVE ID lookup and free-text keyword search, and prefers the newest available CVSS score/severity (v3.1 > v3.0 > v2).

items.title: SPF/DMARC/DKIM record builder
items.description: Generate correctly-formatted SPF, DMARC, and DKIM TXT record strings from simple inputs (allowed senders, policy level, reporting address), the reverse of the existing DNS/email-security checks.
items.rationale: Shipped as an Email Record Builder page with SPF/DMARC/DKIM tabs. SPF and DMARC are fully generated from structured inputs with built-in warnings (SPF 10-lookup limit, empty-sender records, DMARC missing rua, full pct=100 reject). DKIM formats an existing pasted public key into the correct TXT record and record name -- it does not generate a key pair (that's the separate RSA/SSH key pair generator roadmap item).

items.title: Integer base converter
items.description: Convert a number between binary, octal, decimal, and hexadecimal, with live conversion as you type.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated Integer Base Converter page, stdlib-only (int()/bin()/oct()/hex()). Handles negative numbers and same-base prefixes (0x/0b/0o) if included. Live-updates as you type, same no-submit-button pattern as chmod Calculator -- no results-vanishing risk since nothing is gated on a transient flag.

items.title: UUID / ULID generator
items.description: Generate UUIDs (v4) and ULIDs in bulk, with copy-to-clipboard and a CSV export for when a batch of test IDs is needed.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated ID Generator page. UUIDv4 uses Python's stdlib uuid module; ULID has no stdlib equivalent, so it's implemented directly against the spec (48-bit ms timestamp + 80-bit randomness, Crockford Base32, 26 chars) using only stdlib time/secrets -- no new dependency. Also caught and fixed a real bug while building this: st.download_button triggers a script rerun just like any other widget, so a download button inside a block gated on a transient form-submitted flag collapses the whole results section right after the file downloads -- the same bug class as PR #33/#34, now also confirmed present on several older, previously-shipped pages (tracked separately).

items.title: TOTP/OTP code generator and validator
items.description: Generate and validate time-based one-time passcodes (TOTP) from a shared secret, for testing MFA setups without needing a phone in hand.
items.rationale: Shipped as a TOTP Generator page with two tabs: generate a current code from a secret (with a 'generate random secret' button for quick testing), and verify a code against a secret with one 30-second window of clock-drift tolerance. Added pyotp as a new dependency (small, well-established, single-purpose library) -- flagged explicitly since this app has a history of dependency-related incidents.

items.title: Bcrypt hash generator/verifier
items.description: Hash a value with bcrypt (configurable cost factor) and separately verify a value against an existing bcrypt hash.
items.rationale: Shipped as a Bcrypt Tool page with Hash and Verify tabs. Configurable cost factor (4-15 rounds; capped below bcrypt's full range since round 16+ takes several seconds per hash, a DoS concern on a shared public app). Handles both of bcrypt's real error modes: passwords over the library's hard 72-byte limit, and invalid hash strings on verify. Adds bcrypt as a new dependency, verified installing cleanly with no extra transitive packages beyond itself.

items.title: RSA/SSH key pair generator
items.description: Generate an RSA (or ed25519) key pair in the browser for test/throwaway use -- SSH authorized_keys format and PEM private key.
items.rationale: Shipped as an RSA/SSH Key Pair Generator page supporting RSA (2048/3072/4096) and Ed25519, outputting PKCS8 PEM private key + OpenSSH-format public key + SHA256 fingerprint (matches real ssh-keygen -lf output format). Adds cryptography as a new dependency -- widely-used, has prebuilt wheels for standard platforms, no compilation needed. Explicit warning on the page that this is for disposable test credentials only, never anything real, since the app has no way to protect a private key once rendered to the browser.

items.title: chmod calculator
items.description: Convert between symbolic (rwxr-xr--) and octal (754) Unix file permission notation, both directions, with a checkbox grid for building permissions visually.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated chmod Calculator page with three tabs: octal-to-symbolic, symbolic-to-octal, and a visual checkbox-grid builder. Correctly handles setuid/setgid/sticky special bits including the S/T (uppercase) forms when the underlying execute bit is absent -- verified against known real-world examples and round-tripped. Stdlib-only (regex), no dependency. Live-updates as you type with no submit button, so there's no results-vanishing risk (nothing is gated on a transient submit flag).

items.title: Config format converter (YAML / TOML / XML / JSON)
items.description: Convert a pasted config snippet between YAML, TOML, XML, and JSON, reusing the existing JSON Formatter's validation/error-display pattern.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated Config Format Converter page. JSON/YAML/TOML share the same object model and convert losslessly (modulo TOML's own restrictions -- no top-level list, no null). XML has no standard equivalent, so the tool uses one explicit, disclosed convention (keys become child elements, lists become repeated elements, scalars become element text) rather than pretending it's a universal mapping -- called out directly on the page. Added pyyaml to requirements.txt; toml was already a transitive dependency.

items.title: JSON diff viewer
items.description: Structurally diff two JSON documents (key-aware, not line-based) and highlight added/removed/changed fields.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated JSON Diff Viewer page. Structurally diffs by key/path (not by line), so key reordering is not reported as a difference, unlike the existing Text Diff Checker. Walks iteratively with an explicit stack, not recursion, and caps results at 500 -- same defensive pattern already used by json_stats/search_json_paths in utils/text_tools.py for the same reason (a short but deeply-nested JSON string can exceed Python's recursion limit).

items.title: SQL formatter/prettifier
items.description: Reformat a pasted SQL query with consistent indentation and keyword casing for readability.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated SQL Formatter page. sqlparse is a lenient tokenizer/formatter, not a validator for a specific SQL dialect -- it never rejects input as 'invalid SQL' and even uppercases recognized keywords inside otherwise-plain text (confirmed directly, not assumed, and stated on the page itself rather than implying validation that doesn't happen). Adds sqlparse as a new dependency, no transitive packages. Live-updates, no submit button -- no results-vanishing risk. This was the final remaining roadmap backlog item.

items.title: HTTP status code reference
items.description: Searchable static reference of HTTP status codes with meaning and common causes, standalone from the live HTTP Status Checker.
items.rationale: Shipped as a dedicated HTTP Status Reference page, same static-dataset + search shape as Port Reference and the Windows Event/Error References. Covers 39 commonly-seen 1xx-5xx codes, searchable by code, category, or keyword.

items.title: ULID/UUID decoder
items.description: Decode a ULID back to its embedded creation timestamp, or identify a UUID's version and (for v1/v7) extract its embedded timestamp.
items.rationale: Reverse of the existing ID Generator -- useful when you have an ID from a log or database row and want to know when it was created without a lookup. Stdlib-only (struct/datetime), no new dependency.

items.title: .env file linter
items.description: Paste a .env file and flag common mistakes: duplicate keys, unquoted values with spaces, trailing whitespace, missing '=', and accidental export/quote mismatches.
items.rationale: Common DevOps footgun-catcher; distinct from Config Format Converter (which converts between structured formats, not this key=value convention). Stdlib-only, no dependency.

items.title: curl command builder
items.description: Build a copy-pasteable curl command line from a method, URL, headers, and body -- the inverse of Webhook Tester, which executes the request instead of generating the command.
items.rationale: Useful when you want the request to run somewhere else (a script, a teammate's terminal, a support ticket) rather than from this app. Reuses Webhook Tester's header/body parsing helpers where possible.

items.title: CSV diff viewer
items.description: Structurally compare two CSV files by a chosen key column, showing added/removed/changed rows -- the CSV equivalent of the existing JSON Diff Viewer.
items.rationale: Common export-comparison task (before/after a data migration, config export diffing) that a raw text diff handles poorly once rows reorder. Stdlib csv module, no new dependency.

items.title: Regex cheat sheet reference
items.description: Static, searchable reference of common regex patterns (email, IPv4/IPv6, URL, phone number, UUID, hex color, etc.) with a short explanation for each.
items.rationale: Same static-dataset + search shape as Port Reference and the Windows Event/Error References. Complements Regex Tester (which tests a pattern you already have) with patterns to start from.

items.title: Markdown <-> HTML converter
items.description: Convert Markdown to HTML and HTML back to Markdown.
items.rationale: Common content-authoring task (README snippets, ticket notes, wiki pages) not currently covered. Would need a small markdown-to-HTML dependency (e.g. `markdown`) and an HTML-to-Markdown one (e.g. `markdownify`) -- flag both at build time.

items.title: TLS cipher/protocol scanner
items.description: Connect to a host:port and report which TLS protocol versions (SSLv3-TLS1.3) and select cipher suites are accepted or rejected, similar to a lightweight SSL Labs check.
items.rationale: Complements the existing SSL Certificate Checker (which reports the certificate actually presented) with what the server's TLS stack will negotiate. Buildable with stdlib `ssl`/`socket` (multiple connection attempts, one per protocol/cipher-set) -- no new dependency, but each check takes several real network round trips, so needs a sensible cap on how many combinations are probed.

items.title: Business hours / SLA duration calculator
items.description: Compute elapsed business hours between two timestamps, excluding weekends and a configurable set of holidays -- for SLA/response-time tracking.
items.rationale: Directly useful for MSP ticket SLA math, distinct from the existing Timestamp Converter (single-value conversion) and Uptime Trend (uptime %, not elapsed business time). Stdlib datetime only.

items.title: Text encoding detector and converter
items.description: Detect the likely character encoding of pasted or uploaded text (e.g. Windows-1252 vs UTF-8 vs UTF-16) and convert it to clean UTF-8.
items.rationale: Useful for garbled log files or CSV exports from older Windows tools that show mojibake when opened as UTF-8. Would need a small detection dependency (e.g. `charset-normalizer`, already a transitive dependency of `requests`) -- flag at build time whether it's already present.

items.title: robots.txt / sitemap.xml validator
items.description: Fetch a domain's robots.txt and referenced sitemap(s), validate their syntax, and report basic issues (unreachable sitemap URL, malformed directives).
items.rationale: Common pre-launch/SEO-audit check for web developers; reuses the same live-fetch pattern already validated by HTTP Status Checker and Security Headers Checker.

items.title: JWT weak-secret checker
items.description: Test whether a JWT's HMAC signature matches any secret from a small built-in list of common/weak secrets (e.g. 'secret', 'changeme', '123456') -- a quick sanity check for your own tokens, not a general cracking tool.
items.rationale: Complements the existing JWT Decoder/Encoder. Deliberately scoped to a short built-in wordlist (not a brute-force engine or user-supplied wordlist upload) to keep this a quick sanity check rather than something that could be repurposed as an attack tool against third-party tokens.

items.title: Log timestamp duration calculator
items.description: Paste two timestamps (in any of several common log formats -- ISO 8601, syslog, Apache/nginx access log) and get the elapsed duration between them, auto-detecting the format of each.
items.rationale: Common troubleshooting task (how long did this incident/request actually take, from two log lines in different formats) that the existing Timestamp Converter doesn't directly answer since it only converts single values, not computes a delta between two auto-detected formats.

items.title: URL parser / breakdown tool
items.description: Paste a URL and see it broken down into scheme, host, port, path, query parameters (as a table), and fragment.
items.rationale: Distinct from the existing URL Encoder/Decoder (which only percent-encodes/decodes a string) -- this parses structure. Common need when debugging a long URL with many query params pasted from a browser or log line. Buildable with stdlib urllib.parse only, no new dependency. Verified directly: urllib.parse.urlsplit/parse_qsl handle scheme/host/port/path/query/fragment cleanly.

items.title: Base32 encoder/decoder
items.description: Encode/decode text or bytes to/from Base32 (RFC 4648), the encoding TOTP secrets and some other systems use.
items.rationale: Distinct from Base64 Tool (different alphabet/encoding) and Integer Base Converter (which converts numbers between numeric bases, not byte encoding). Directly complements the existing TOTP Generator, which already consumes Base32 secrets. Stdlib base64.b32encode/b32decode only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: Raw HTTP header parser
items.description: Paste a raw block of HTTP request or response headers (e.g. copied from browser devtools) and see them parsed into a labeled table with brief explanations for well-known headers.
items.rationale: Distinct from Security Headers Checker and HTTP Status Checker, both of which fetch headers live from a URL -- this parses headers a user already has in hand (from devtools, a support ticket, a curl -v output) with no network call at all. Stdlib text parsing only, no new dependency.

items.title: CIDR overlap checker
items.description: Enter two or more CIDR ranges and check whether any of them overlap.
items.rationale: Complements the existing Subnet Calculator and CIDR Aggregator (which describe/merge ranges but don't flag overlap between separately-entered ranges) -- a common pre-flight check before allocating a new subnet block. Stdlib ipaddress.ip_network(...).overlaps() only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: CSR decoder
items.description: Paste a PEM-encoded Certificate Signing Request (CSR) and see its subject, SAN entries, public key algorithm/size, and signature validity.
items.rationale: Complements SSL Certificate Checker (which inspects an issued cert, not the request that preceded it) and RSA/SSH Key Pair Generator. Uses the `cryptography` package already installed for this app's TOTP/keypair/bcrypt tools -- x509.load_pem_x509_csr() and CSR.is_signature_valid -- no new dependency. Verified directly by generating and parsing a real CSR.

items.title: PEM certificate bundle splitter
items.description: Paste a multi-certificate PEM bundle (e.g. a full chain file) and see it split into individual certificates, each with its subject, issuer, and expiration shown separately.
items.rationale: Complements SSL Certificate Checker -- a common troubleshooting need when a server's chain file has certs in the wrong order or an unexpected extra/missing intermediate, which is hard to eyeball from one long PEM blob. Uses the `cryptography` package already installed (x509.load_pem_x509_certificates), no new dependency.

items.title: Invisible/whitespace character visualizer
items.description: Paste text and highlight non-breaking spaces, tabs, zero-width characters, and other invisible/lookalike characters that commonly cause silent copy-paste bugs (e.g. in config files or scripts).
items.rationale: A common, hard-to-self-diagnose class of bug (a config value that 'looks' right but has a stray non-breaking space or zero-width character pasted in from a rich-text source). Stdlib only -- iterate codepoints and flag anything outside printable ASCII plus common accented text.

items.title: Date calculator
items.description: Add or subtract a number of days/weeks/months from a date, or compute the number of calendar days between two dates.
items.rationale: Distinct from Timestamp Converter (single-value epoch/ISO conversion), Business Hours Calculator (business-hours-only elapsed time), and Log Timestamp Duration Calculator (log-format auto-detection) -- this is plain calendar-date arithmetic (e.g. 'what date is 90 days from now', 'how many days until this deadline'), a different and more common everyday need. Stdlib datetime.timedelta only, no new dependency.

items.title: XML formatter/validator
items.description: Paste XML and get it pretty-printed with consistent indentation, or flagged with a clear error if it's not well-formed.
items.rationale: Distinct from JSON Formatter and Config Format Converter's XML support (which only converts a JSON-shaped object model to a simple XML convention, not general XML with attributes/mixed content/namespaces) -- this formats/validates arbitrary XML as-is. Stdlib xml.dom.minidom.toprettyxml, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: HTML entity encoder/decoder
items.description: Encode text to HTML entities (<, &, ", etc.) or decode HTML entities back to plain text.
items.rationale: Distinct from URL Encoder/Decoder and Base64/Base32 Tools (different encoding entirely) -- a common need when embedding user text in HTML or debugging entity-encoded content copied from a web page. Stdlib html.escape/html.unescape only, no new dependency -- verified directly, including numeric character references.

items.title: Deterministic UUID generator (v3/v5)
items.description: Generate a namespace-based UUID (v3 MD5 or v5 SHA-1) from a namespace + name pair -- the same input always produces the same UUID.
items.rationale: Distinct from the existing ID Generator, which only generates random v1/v4/v7 UUIDs -- v3/v5 are deterministic/hash-based, useful for generating stable IDs from external identifiers (e.g. a URL or DNS name) without a database. Stdlib uuid.uuid3/uuid5 with the 4 standard namespaces (DNS, URL, OID, X.500), no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: Luhn checksum validator
items.description: Validate a credit card number, IMEI, or other Luhn-checksummed number, and optionally compute the correct check digit for a partial number.
items.rationale: Common quick-validation need (did I mistype a card/IMEI number) with no existing tool covering it. Stdlib arithmetic only, no new dependency -- verified directly against a known-valid test card number.

items.title: Text statistics / word frequency counter
items.description: Paste text and see word count, character count, sentence count, and the most frequent words.
items.rationale: No existing general-purpose text-stats tool -- JSON Formatter's stats are JSON-structure-specific, not applicable to plain prose/logs. Stdlib re + collections.Counter only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: CSV to Markdown table converter
items.description: Paste CSV (or TSV) and get a Markdown table, ready to paste into a README, PR description, or wiki page.
items.rationale: Complements CSV Diff Viewer and Markdown/HTML Converter, but distinct from both -- this is a common one-off formatting task (turning a spreadsheet export into a Markdown table) with no existing tool. Stdlib csv module only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: SSH key fingerprint tool
items.description: Paste a public SSH key (or a known_hosts line) and see its MD5 and SHA256 fingerprints, matching the format ssh-keygen -lf prints.
items.rationale: Complements the existing RSA/SSH Key Pair Generator -- useful for verifying a key you already have against a fingerprint shown elsewhere (e.g. a GitHub deploy key or server host key). Uses the `cryptography` package already installed for this app's other key/cert tools, no new dependency -- verified directly against a freshly generated key, matching ssh-keygen's known fingerprint format.

items.title: YAML formatter/validator
items.description: Paste YAML and get it consistently re-indented, or flagged with a clear error and line number if it's not valid YAML.
items.rationale: Distinct from Config Format Converter's YAML support (which only converts a JSON-shaped object model between formats, not format/validate YAML as-is) -- same relationship XML Formatter already has to Config Format Converter's XML support. Uses `pyyaml`, already an installed dependency, no new pin -- verified directly including a malformed-input error with line/column.

items.title: Byte size converter
items.description: Convert a byte count into human-readable units (KB/MB/GB/TB, both decimal-1000-based and binary-1024-based), or the reverse.
items.rationale: Common sysadmin need (interpreting a raw byte count from a log, df output, or API response) with no existing tool -- distinct from Integer Base Converter, which converts numeric bases, not units. Stdlib arithmetic only, no new dependency -- verified directly for both binary and decimal unit systems.

items.title: Line ending converter
items.description: Convert pasted text between CRLF (Windows), LF (Unix/Mac), and CR (classic Mac) line endings.
items.rationale: Common cross-platform text/config file issue (e.g. a script that fails silently because of Windows line endings) with no existing tool covering it directly. Stdlib string replacement only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: Regex find & replace
items.description: Paste text and a regex pattern with a replacement (including backreferences like \1), and see the substituted output.
items.rationale: Distinct from Regex Tester (which only shows match/no-match and capture groups, not a substituted result) -- a common need when constructing a find/replace regex before using it in a script or editor. Stdlib re.sub only, no new dependency -- verified directly including backreference substitution.

items.title: Password strength / entropy checker
items.description: Paste a password and see an estimated entropy (bits) and rough strength category, based on character-set diversity and length.
items.rationale: Distinct from the existing Password Generator (which creates new passwords, not scores existing ones) -- useful for checking a password you already have in mind. Deliberately scoped to a straightforward character-pool-based entropy estimate (not a dictionary/pattern-based cracking-time model, which would need an external wordlist/library) so it stays honest about what it measures. Stdlib math only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: Text pattern extractor (grep-style)
items.description: Paste text and a regex pattern, and get back only the matching lines (or captured groups), like a grep -E over pasted text.
items.rationale: Distinct from Regex Tester (single-string match/no-match) and Log Troubleshooting Assistant (fixed known-issue patterns, not a user-supplied pattern) -- a common need when scanning a pasted log or config for lines matching an arbitrary pattern. Stdlib re only, no new dependency -- verified directly.

items.title: CSV / JSON converter
items.description: Convert CSV/TSV (with a header row) to a JSON array of objects, or the reverse.
items.rationale: Distinct from Config Format Converter (handles JSON/YAML/TOML/XML, no CSV) and CSV to Markdown Table (one-way, CSV to Markdown only). Stdlib csv+json only, no new dependency -- verified directly, including a round-trip CSV->JSON->CSV check.

items.title: Sort & dedupe lines
items.description: Sort pasted text's lines, remove duplicates, and/or drop blank lines -- like sort -u over pasted text.
items.rationale: Distinct from Text Diff Checker (compares two texts) and CSV/TSV Cleaner (structured rows/cells, not arbitrary lines). Stdlib only, no new dependency -- verified directly, including numeric and case-insensitive sort modes.

items.title: User-Agent builder
items.description: Build a User-Agent string for a chosen OS, browser, and version -- the reverse of User Agent Parser.
items.rationale: User Agent Parser only decomposes an existing UA string; this fills the reverse need (testing how a site responds to a specific browser without switching devices). Rejects OS/browser combinations that never existed in the real world (e.g. Safari on Windows). Stdlib only, no new dependency.

items.title: SemVer comparator / sorter
items.description: Compare two Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version strings, or sort a whole list by precedence.
items.rationale: Uses the official SemVer 2.0.0 regex and precedence rules published at semver.org, verified directly against the spec's own worked precedence-order example (1.0.0-alpha < ... < 1.0.0). Stdlib re only, no new dependency -- deliberately not using the packaging library's version comparator, which implements PEP 440, not SemVer.

items.title: World clock / meeting time planner
items.description: See one date/time across major world timezones -- useful for planning a meeting or a maintenance window.
items.rationale: Distinct from Timestamp Converter's convert_timezone (a single from/to conversion) -- shows every zone in a curated list side by side at once. Stdlib zoneinfo only, no new dependency.

items.title: CSV/TSV cleaner
items.description: Paste messy CSV/TSV and trim cell whitespace, drop empty rows, and/or remove duplicate rows.
items.rationale: Distinct from Sort & Dedupe Lines (arbitrary text lines, not structured rows/cells) and CSV Diff Viewer (compares two CSVs, doesn't clean one). Stdlib csv only, no new dependency.

items.title: JSON Path query (simple dotted path)
items.description: Extract a value from JSON with a simple dotted path, e.g. user.addresses[0].city.
items.rationale: Deliberately scoped to dotted keys and [index] array access only -- no wildcards, filters, or slicing -- so it stays honest about not being a full JSONPath/JMESPath implementation and doesn't need a new dependency. Distinct from JSON Diff Viewer (structural comparison) and JSON Formatter (pretty-print/minify).

items.title: IBAN validator
items.description: Check an IBAN's structure (country-specific length) and mod-97 checksum.
items.rationale: Distinct algorithm from Luhn Checksum Validator (card numbers). Verified the mod-97 implementation and the country-length table directly against known-valid published IBAN test vectors (Germany, UK) before shipping. Stdlib only, no new dependency.

items.title: Base58 encoder/decoder
items.description: Encode or decode text using the Bitcoin/IPFS Base58 alphabet (excludes 0, O, I, l).
items.rationale: Distinct from Base32/Base64 Tool (different alphabet and algorithm) and Integer Base Converter (arbitrary numeric base 2-16 of a single integer, not this specific alphabet/leading-zero-byte handling). Verified against the well-known 'Hello World' and Bitcoin-address Base58 test vectors before shipping. Stdlib only, no new dependency.

items.title: Exit code reference (Linux/Bash)
items.description: Look up Linux/Bash process exit codes -- a quick lookup when a script or CI job fails with an unfamiliar code.
items.rationale: Matches the established static-reference pattern (HTTP Status Reference, Windows Error Reference, Port Reference). Deliberately limits itself to codes with a universally-documented meaning (0-2, 126-165) rather than implying 3-125 mean something specific, since those are application-defined.

items.title: Timezone abbreviation reference
items.description: Look up timezone abbreviations (EST, IST, CST...) and their UTC offset.
items.rationale: Handles a well-documented real-world hazard head-on: many abbreviations (CST, IST, BST) are genuinely ambiguous with multiple real meanings at different UTC offsets, so every meaning is listed as its own row instead of picking one. Distinct from World Clock (interactive conversion of a specific date/time).

items.title: HTTP Basic Auth header tool
items.description: Build or parse an HTTP Authorization: Basic header (RFC 7617).
items.rationale: Distinct from Base64 Tool (generic encode/decode, no credential-format awareness) and HTTP Header Parser (parses a whole raw header block, not specifically this format). Rejects a colon in the username on build, since RFC 7617 uses the first colon as the user-id/password separator.

items.title: .gitignore pattern tester
items.description: Paste .gitignore content and test whether specific paths would be ignored.
items.rationale: Implements gitignore's core glob semantics (*, ?, [...], **, leading/trailing /, ! negation). The anchoring rules and ** zero-directory matching are notoriously easy to get wrong -- verified every rule directly against real `git check-ignore` output before shipping, and caught two real bugs in the draft implementation this way (an over-anchoring bug and a **-doesn't-match-zero-dirs bug). Deliberately doesn't implement git's parent-directory-blocks-reinclusion rule, since that needs a real directory tree, not a single path string -- disclosed in the page's warning.

items.title: Markdown table of contents generator
items.description: Paste Markdown and get a linked table of contents built from its headings.
items.rationale: Anchor slugs follow GitHub's actual algorithm, verified against GitHub's real rendered anchors for punctuation and duplicate headings. Distinct from Markdown/HTML Converter (format conversion, no TOC). Caught a real bug in the draft heading-closer regex (a heading literally ending in '#', like 'C#', had its trailing character wrongly stripped as a closing ATX sequence) before shipping.

items.title: Number to words
items.description: Spell out an integer in English words, e.g. 1042 -> one thousand forty-two.
items.rationale: Deliberately one direction only (number -> words) -- parsing loosely formatted English text back into a number is ambiguous in a way the forward direction isn't. Caught a real bug in the draft scale-word list (it skipped "quadrillion" entirely, mislabeling larger numbers and crashing at the largest supported magnitude) via direct testing before shipping.

items.title: JSON to TypeScript interface generator
items.description: Infer a TypeScript interface from a JSON document, with nested objects broken out into their own interfaces.
items.rationale: Distinct from JSON Formatter (pretty-print only, no type inference). Nested objects get their own named interface; an empty array is typed unknown[] rather than guessed, since its element type genuinely can't be inferred from the data.

items.title: CSS gradient generator
items.description: Build a linear-gradient() or radial-gradient() CSS declaration from a list of hex color stops.
items.rationale: Distinct from Color Converter (single-color format conversion, not a multi-stop gradient declaration). A live preview swatch was considered but dropped after review found it would have embedded an unvalidated free-text field (angle/shape) directly into an HTML style attribute via unsafe_allow_html -- a real injection risk removed before shipping rather than patched around.

items.title: JWT claims reference
items.description: Look up what a JWT claim name means -- registered (RFC 7519) claims plus common OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect conventions.
items.rationale: Standalone from JWT Decoder/Encoder -- useful when you just need to remember what a claim name means without decoding a real token. Registered vs. common-but-unstandardized claims are labeled separately so this doesn't imply a false standardization.

items.title: CSP header builder
items.description: Build a Content-Security-Policy header value from directives and source lists, entirely locally.
items.rationale: Distinct from Security Headers Checker (fetches a live URL and checks whether a CSP is present/reasonable, doesn't build one). Known CSP keyword sources ('self', 'none', 'unsafe-inline', etc.) are auto-quoted per spec; anything else is left unquoted, since CSP only quotes its own reserved keywords.

items.title: Robots meta tag builder
items.description: Build a <meta name="robots" content="..."> tag -- distinct from robots.txt, which applies site-wide.
items.rationale: Distinct from robots.txt / Sitemap Validator (validates a site's robots.txt file, a separate mechanism, fetched live) -- this builds the per-page HTML meta tag, entirely locally, following Google's documented robots meta tag values.

items.title: Cache-Control tool
items.description: Build a Cache-Control header from directives, or paste one to see each directive explained.
items.rationale: Distinct from HTTP Header Parser (generic header block parsing, no per-directive explanations). Rejects contradictory combinations (public+private, no-store+max-age) rather than silently building a nonsensical header.

items.title: Markdown table formatter
items.description: Paste a Markdown table with ragged/misaligned columns and get it re-aligned to consistent, padded widths.
items.rationale: Distinct from CSV to Markdown Table (builds a table from CSV, doesn't reformat an existing Markdown table). Preserves each column's alignment marker (:---, ---:, :---:, ---) from the existing separator row.

items.title: CSV column selector
items.description: Extract and reorder specific columns from CSV/TSV by header name.
items.rationale: Distinct from CSV/TSV Cleaner (trims/dedupes rows and cells, doesn't select/reorder columns) and CSV to Markdown Table (converts everything, no column selection).

items.title: HTTP methods reference
items.description: Look up HTTP methods and their safe/idempotent/cacheable properties per RFC 9110.
items.rationale: Standalone from HTTP Status Checker/Reference -- methods and status codes are different axes of the HTTP spec. Safe/idempotent/cacheable are the three properties most often gotten wrong in practice (e.g. PUT being idempotent surprises people used to thinking only GET is safe); POST's conditional cacheability is called out explicitly rather than flattened to a plain No.

items.title: Line numberer
items.description: Add line numbers to pasted text -- handy for referencing a specific line in a review or bug report.
items.rationale: No existing tool numbers arbitrary pasted text lines. Right-aligns numbers to the widest needed width so columns stay lined up regardless of line count.

items.title: PII redactor
items.description: Redact common sensitive-looking patterns from pasted text before sharing it in a ticket, log, or chat.
items.rationale: Regex-based heuristics, explicitly disclosed as such -- not a real PII detector. All patterns matched in a single combined pass, with the broad credit-card pattern tried last so it can't swallow a more specific SSN/phone match sitting inside a longer digit run (verified directly).

items.title: .env file diff
items.description: Compare two .env files and see which keys were added, removed, or changed.
items.rationale: Distinct from .env File Linter (checks one file for mistakes, doesn't compare two) and JSON/CSV Diff (different formats). Parsing mirrors env_linter's own conventions (export prefix, first '=' as separator) for consistency.

items.title: Cron overlap checker
items.description: Check whether two cron schedules ever fire in the same minute -- useful for spotting jobs that might contend for the same resource.
items.rationale: Distinct from Cron Explainer/Builder (single-schedule tools). Reuses croniter (already a dependency). Hard-caps occurrences per schedule so a once-a-minute schedule combined with a long lookahead window can't turn into an unbounded loop.

items.title: Test data generator
items.description: Generate fake names, emails, usernames, and phone numbers for filling in forms and test fixtures.
items.rationale: Uses IANA-reserved example domains (RFC 2606) for emails and the North American 555-01XX fictional-use phone range, so nothing generated can collide with a real address. Optional seed for reproducible test fixtures.

items.title: Password policy checker
items.description: Check a password against a configurable complexity policy -- pass/fail per rule, not an entropy estimate.
items.rationale: Distinct from Password Strength Checker (continuous entropy estimate) and Password Generator (creates new passwords) -- this checks pass/fail compliance against explicit, configurable rules, the kind an org sets for its users.

items.title: ISO 8601 duration tool
items.description: Parse an ISO 8601 duration (e.g. P3Y6M4DT12H30M5S) into plain English, or build one from individual units.
items.rationale: Distinct from Timestamp Converter/Log Timestamp Duration Calculator, which work with actual timestamps, not the ISO 8601 duration format used in many APIs and config files (AWS, Kubernetes, iCalendar).

items.title: JSON merge patch
items.description: Merge two JSON documents per RFC 7396 -- useful for layering an environment-specific override onto a base config.
items.rationale: Distinct from JSON Diff Viewer (compares, doesn't combine) and JSON Path Query (extracts, doesn't merge). Verified directly against all 15 of RFC 7396's own Appendix A test cases before shipping.

items.title: Column aligner
items.description: Align whitespace-separated columns of plain text -- like the Unix column -t command.
items.rationale: Distinct from Markdown Table Formatter (pipe-delimited Markdown tables) and CSV Column Selector (comma-delimited, selects/reorders rather than aligns). Meant for pasted command output (ps aux, df -h) with ragged spacing.

items.title: SSH config validator
items.description: Lint ~/.ssh/config content for structural mistakes -- directives before any Host block, empty Host blocks, duplicate Host patterns.
items.rationale: Checks structure only, not individual directive names -- OpenSSH has ~100 valid ssh_config keywords, and an incomplete allowlist would flag valid but less common ones as errors.

items.title: CSR generator
items.description: Generate a new RSA key pair and a Certificate Signing Request from subject fields -- the reverse of CSR Decoder.
items.rationale: Verified the generated CSR round-trips correctly through the existing CSR Decoder (valid signature, correct subject/SAN fields) before shipping. Same disposable/test-use framing as RSA/SSH Key Pair Generator -- this app can't protect a private key once rendered to the browser.

items.title: CAA record builder
items.description: Build a DNS CAA (Certification Authority Authorization) record, restricting which CAs may issue certificates for a domain.
items.rationale: A different DNS record type (RFC 8659) from Email Record Builder's SPF/DMARC/DKIM, not covered by any existing tool.
